# P09 — Ruth 3:6-13

## 1. Metadata
- **Pericope title:** The threshing-floor night: the wing asked for, the word redeemer spoken, the oath
- **BCV:** Ruth 3:6-13
- **Genre Group:** NARRATIVE
- **Genre:** HISTORICAL_NARRATIVE
- **Register:** INFORMAL_CASUAL

*(Versification note: Ruth's chapter and verse numbers are the same in English and Hebrew — no divergence in this pericope.)*

**Multi-level register tagging:**
The whole passage sits in INFORMAL_CASUAL. Scenes 2 and 3 shift to CONSULTATIVE: a respectful exchange between the two of them, alone, at night. Boaz's blessing at v.10 ("blessed are you of YHWH, my daughter") and his oath at v.13 ("as YHWH lives") keep their exact formula wording; neither carries a register shift of its own. Scene 1 is the narrator's plain telling.

## 2. Level 1 — Whole-Passage Movement

### 2.1 Prose Arc / Shape / Argument / Burden / Concern
The passage walks Naomi's plan into the dark and out the other side, changed. Ruth goes down to the floor and does all her mother-in-law commanded. Boaz eats and drinks, his heart is good, and he lies down at the end of the grain heap; she comes softly, uncovers the place of his feet, and lies down. At half of the night the man trembles, twists — and there is a woman lying at his feet. He asks who she is. She answers with her name and more than the plan gave her: I am Ruth your servant — spread your wing over your servant, for you are a redeemer. Naomi's plan said he would tell her what to do; in the night it is Ruth who makes the request. Boaz answers with a blessing — blessed are you of YHWH, my daughter — and calls this her last hesed (loyal, covenant kindness), better than the first: she has not gone after the young men, poor or rich. He quiets her fear, gives back her own words from the plan's first scene — all that you say I will do for you — and gives the reason: the whole gate of my people knows you are a woman of worth. Then the turn no one planned for: truly I am a redeemer — but there is a redeemer nearer than I. He sets the morning's protocol — if he redeems you, good, let him redeem; if he does not want to, I will redeem you myself — and seals it with the oath: as YHWH lives. Lie down until the morning. What weighs on the passage is how much hangs on the night's words — a promise bound under oath, and a redeemer nearer than Boaz who comes first — and the question it leaves open is which of the two will redeem her in the morning.

### 2.2 Context
This follows Naomi's plan (3:1–5). Naomi's plan said he would tell Ruth what to do (3:4); in the night it is Ruth who makes the request (3:9), and Boaz answers and sends the next step to the morning (3:13). The narrator does not comment on the change. In her request she uses the same word Boaz used at 2:12 for the wings of YHWH: at 2:12 he blessed her under the wings (kanaf) of the God of Israel; at 3:9 she says, spread your wing (kanaf) over your servant. The word redeemer, not said in Naomi's plan (at 3:2 she called him "our kinsman"), is said now — by Ruth, in the dark, as the reason for her request. Boaz's "last hesed better than the first" reaches back through the book's hesed-thread (1:8; 2:20); Boaz does not say which the first was, and he names the last by what she did not do: go after the young men, poor or rich. His "woman of worth" (eshet chayil) completes the pair the narrator opened at 2:1, where Boaz entered as a man of worth (ish gibbor chayil). And his disclosure brings back 2:20's "one of our redeemers": there is a redeemer nearer than Boaz, who comes first because he is nearer.

### 2.3 Emotion / Tone / Pace
The first scene is all quiet motion — eating, drinking, a good heart, lying down, soft footsteps, an uncovering, a lying down — told plainly and fast. The midnight startle snaps the stillness: a tremble, a twist, a woman lying at his feet. Then the pace stops moving and the talk takes over, and much hangs on it: her one sentence asking for everything; his answer unrolling slowly — blessing, praise, reassurance, complication, oath. The held breath of the passage is the gap between "you are a redeemer" and "there is a redeemer nearer than I." It ends with the strange calm of a settled protocol: lie down until the morning.

### 2.4 Communicative Function
This passage is the hinge of the book: the wing-word Boaz used at 2:12 returns in Ruth's request; the assent-words of 3:5 come back in Boaz's mouth; Naomi's plan said he would tell her what to do, and in the night it is Ruth who makes the request. It puts the word redeemer in Ruth's mouth for the first time, and Boaz at once adds that there is a redeemer nearer than he. It fixes Ruth's public standing — a woman of worth, known to all the gate of his people — matching her to Boaz's own introduction. It binds the night's promise under the oath "as YHWH lives". To speak this passage is to keep the exchange between the two of them, the exact words of the blessing and the oath, and both of the morning's possibilities: if the nearer redeemer redeems, good; if he is not willing, Boaz will.

## 3. Level 2 — Scenes / Episodes

### Scene 1 — Down to the floor; the uncovering (3:6–7)

**3A — Beings**

[[B9-Ruth]] — רוּת / Ruth
- Role: the one who goes down, does all as commanded, comes softly, uncovers, and lies down
- Relationship: Moabite daughter-in-law of [[B3-Naomi]] Naomi; acting on her plan
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B13-Boaz]] — בֹּעַז / Boaz
- Role: the one who eats and drinks, whose heart is good, and who lies down by the grain
- Relationship: the kinsman Naomi named (3:2); he does not yet know she is there
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B3-Naomi]] — חֲמוֹתָהּ / "her mother-in-law"
- Role: the absent planner whose command Ruth carries out
- Relationship: mother-in-law of [[B9-Ruth]] Ruth
- Presence: REFERENCED

**3B — Places**

[[PL6-Threshing-Floor]] — הַגֹּרֶן / the threshing floor
- Role: the scene of the whole night
- Type: the open working-floor at winnowing time; Boaz lies down by the grain heap
- Effect on scene: the place the plan named, now entered

[[PL_END_OF_GRAIN_HEAP-End-of-the-Grain-Heap]] — קְצֵה הָעֲרֵמָה / "the end of the grain heap"
- Role: where Boaz lies down
- Type: the edge of the piled grain on the floor
- Effect on scene: fixes the place Ruth must find in the dark

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

[[CB_0042-Uncover-Feet-Margelot]] — מַרְגְּלֹתָיו / "the place of his feet"
- What it is: the place of his feet (margelot); the text says only that she uncovers it
- Function in scene: the act the plan ordered, now done: she comes softly, uncovers the place of his feet, and lies down

**3D — Times**
- None as a distinct frame: the scene runs from the evening meal into the night; the night itself is marked at the next scene's startle.

**3E — What Happens**
[[B9-Ruth]] Ruth goes down to the [[PL6-Threshing-Floor]] threshing floor and does according to all that her mother-in-law commanded her. [[B13-Boaz]] Boaz eats and drinks, and his heart is good; he comes to lie down at the end of the grain heap. She comes softly, uncovers the place of his feet, and lies down.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
Executes the plan to the letter and sets the night's stage: the man lying down at the end of the grain heap, the woman at his feet, and nothing yet said.

**Significant Absence**
The narrator does not say what Ruth intends beyond the plan. No word is spoken in the whole scene.

### Scene 2 — Midnight: the startle, the question, the request (3:8–9)

**3A — Beings**

[[B13-Boaz]] — הָאִישׁ / "the man"
- Role: the startled man who finds a woman at his feet and asks who she is
- Relationship: not yet told who she is; named only "the man" at the startle
- Referential form: "the man" at v.8; Boaz's name rests until his answer
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B9-Ruth]] — רוּת אֲמָתֶךָ / "Ruth your servant"
- Role: the woman at his feet who names herself and asks for the wing
- Relationship: Moabite daughter-in-law of [[B3-Naomi]] Naomi; she names herself his servant (amah)
- Referential form: "a woman" to the startled man; then by her own mouth, "Ruth your servant" — amah (at 2:13 she called herself shifchah, another word for servant); the text does not say what the change of word means
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B18-The-Redeemer]] — גֹאֵל / "a redeemer"
- Role: the role Ruth names Boaz into — the ground of her request
- Relationship: the near-kinsman duty of [[B2-Elimelech]] Elimelech's line; [[B13-Boaz]] Boaz holds it
- Presence: REFERENCED

**3B — Places**

[[PL6-Threshing-Floor]] — implied
- Role: the dark floor where the exchange happens
- Type: the open working-floor at midnight
- Effect on scene: the two of them alone at the floor, at night

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

[[CB_0037-Refuge-Under-Wings-Kanaph]] — כְנָפֶךָ / "your wing"
- What it is: kanaph, "wing" — the same word names the edge of a garment; to spread it over a woman is to ask for the protection of marriage
- Function in scene: Ruth asks Boaz to spread his wing over his servant; in her line the word is "wing"
- Cross-ref: she uses the same word Boaz used at 2:12 for the wings of YHWH; the pair closes here with her request

[[CB_0001-Kinsman-Redeemer]] — גֹאֵל / "a redeemer"
- What it is: the kinsman-redeemer — a near relative bound to step in for a dead clansman's family, land, and name
- Function in scene: said by Ruth, as the reason for her request
- Cross-ref: named "one of our redeemers" at 2:20; the redeemer word enters Ruth's own mouth here

**3D — Times**

[[TM_MIDDLE_OF_THE_NIGHT-Middle-of-the-Night]] — בַּחֲצִי הַלַּיְלָה / "at half of the night"
- What it is: midnight — the middle of the night
- Function: the time-anchor of the startle; the request is made in the deepest dark

**3E — What Happens**
At half of the night [[B13-Boaz]] the man trembles and twists — and behold, a woman lying at the place of his feet. He says: who are you? [[B9-Ruth]] She says: I am Ruth your servant. Spread your wing over your servant, for you are a redeemer.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
The turn of the night: the plan's script runs out and Ruth speaks past it — name, petition, and the redeemer-claim, in one breath in the dark.

**Significant Absence**
Ruth does not wait for the man to tell her what to do, though Naomi's plan said he would (3:4); in the night it is Ruth who makes the request, and the narrator does not comment on the change. What the uncovering and the lying down mean is never said. No word of love or desire is spoken by either of them.

### Scene 3 — Boaz's answer: blessing, pledge, the nearer redeemer, the oath (3:10–13)

**3A — Beings**

[[B13-Boaz]] — בֹּעַז / Boaz
- Role: the one who blesses, praises, reassures, complicates, and swears
- Relationship: a redeemer of the household — and not the nearest
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B9-Ruth]] — בִּתִּי / "my daughter"
- Role: the one blessed, praised as a woman of worth, and told to lie down until morning
- Relationship: addressed twice as "my daughter" — the same address Naomi uses
- Referential form: "my daughter" in Boaz's mouth; "a woman of worth" (eshet chayil), known to all the gate of his people
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B10-YHWH]] — יְהוָה / YHWH
- Role: the one the blessing invokes, and the one the oath swears by
- Relationship: the God under whose wings, Boaz said at 2:12, she had come to take refuge; now invoked over his own pledge
- Presence: REFERENCED

[[B19-NEARER_REDEEMER_UNNAMED]] — גֹּאֵל קָרוֹב מִמֶּנִּי / "a redeemer nearer than I"
- Role: a redeemer nearer than Boaz, who comes first because he is nearer; unnamed here
- Relationship: a kinsman of [[B2-Elimelech]] Elimelech's line, nearer than Boaz
- Referential form: unnamed here — only "a redeemer nearer than I"
- Presence: REFERENCED

[[B21-All-the-People-at-the-Gate]] — כָּל־שַׁעַר עַמִּי / "all the gate of my people"
- Role: the public whose knowledge of Ruth's worth Boaz cites
- Relationship: the townspeople who know Ruth — "all the gate of my people" in Boaz's words
- Presence: REFERENCED

[[B32-Young-Men-Ruth-Did-Not-Go-After]] — הַבַּחוּרִים / "the young men"
- Role: named in Boaz's praise: the ones Ruth did not go after
- Relationship: the young men, poor or rich, whom Ruth did not go after
- Presence: REFERENCED

**3B — Places**

[[PL6-Threshing-Floor]] — implied
- Role: the dark floor holding the whole answer
- Type: the open working-floor at night
- Effect on scene: the two of them alone at the floor, at night

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

[[CB_0008-Blessing]] — בְּרוּכָה אַתְּ לַיהוָה / "blessed are you of YHWH"
- What it is: a blessing in a fixed formula
- Function in scene: Boaz's first word back — the night's request answered first with blessing; its formula wording is kept exactly

[[CB_0011-Hesed]] — חַסְדֵּךְ / "your hesed"
- What it is: hesed — loyal, covenant kindness that holds people to one another beyond bare duty
- Function in scene: how Boaz names what Ruth has just done — her last hesed, better than the first
- Cross-ref: the thread runs 1:8 and 2:20; here Boaz compares her last hesed with the first and does not say which the first was; the last he names by what she did not do — go after the young men, poor or rich

[[CB_0032-Chayil]] — אֵשֶׁת חַיִל / "a woman of worth"
- What it is: chayil — substance, standing, capability, worth
- Function in scene: Ruth's public standing in Boaz's mouth — what all the gate of his people knows
- Cross-ref: completes the pair with Boaz's own introduction at 2:1, a man of worth

[[CB_0001-Kinsman-Redeemer]] — גֹאֵל / "redeemer"
- What it is: the kinsman-redeemer duty
- Function in scene: Boaz owns the role — truly I am a redeemer — and discloses the nearer one; the redeem-word then runs through the morning protocol, redeem upon redeem

**3D — Times**

[[TM_NIGHT_UNTIL_MORNING-Night-Until-Morning]] — הַלַּיְלָה … בַבֹּקֶר / "the night … in the morning"
- What it is: the night, and the morning named in Boaz's promise
- Function: the promise's two times — lodge the night; in the morning, if the nearer redeemer redeems, good; if he is not willing, Boaz will

**3E — What Happens**
[[B13-Boaz]] Boaz says: blessed are you of [[B10-YHWH]] YHWH, my daughter. You have made your last hesed better than the first — not going after the young men, whether poor or rich. And now, my daughter, do not fear; all that you say I will do for you, for all the gate of my people knows that you are a woman of worth. And now — truly I am a redeemer; but there is also a redeemer nearer than I. Lodge the night; in the morning, if he redeems you — good, let him redeem; and if he does not want to redeem you, then I will redeem you myself — as YHWH lives. Lie down until the morning.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
Answers the night's petition with everything at once — blessing, honor, pledge, and law: Ruth is praised and promised, the nearer redeemer is disclosed, and the whole matter is bound under oath and handed to the morning.

**Significant Absence**
Boaz answers yes to the request ("all that you say I will do") but binds the promise to the order of redeemers: if the nearer one redeems, good; if he is not willing, Boaz himself will redeem, under oath by YHWH. The text does not say which of the two will act, nor what Boaz feels or wants. The nearer redeemer is not named. The narrator reports no touch beyond the uncovering and no word of love or desire; the night passes in words. The text gives no verdict on the night — neither that something happened nor that nothing did.
